To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mitochondrial respiratory chain is the main source of reactive oxygen species ( ROS ) and that the accumulation of oxidative damage in mitochondrial proteins, DNA, and lipids contributes to the aging process.
Oxidative damage to mitochondrial DNA, proteins, and lipids increases with aging and is likely a major contributor to mitochondrial dysfunction and the pathophysiology of aging.

1) the mitochondria are the main source of reactive oxygen species (oxidative stress) in the cell; and 2) the mitochondria, due to oxidative stress, undergo changes with age, including a reduction in mitochondrial number and an increase in oxidative damage to mitochondrial DNA, RNA, lipids, and proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular and cellular events that occur in the mitochondria during the process of aging.
the role of oxidative damage to mitochondrial DNA in the pathophysiology of aging.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of aging and their relationship with the development of diseases associated with the aging process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitochondria of aging cells have lost the ability to maintain the delicate balance between the generation of ROS and their removal by the antioxidant defense systems.
oxidative damage to mitochondria is a key factor in the aging process, and that this damage is a major cause of age-associated degenerative diseases.
the role of oxidative damage to mitochondria is not clear, although it is possible that oxidative damage to mitochondrion is one of the causes of aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mitochondria are a major target for oxidative damage in aging and that this is likely to be a key factor contributing to the pathobiological mechanisms that underlie the loss of function that occurs with age and in degenerative diseases.
oxidative stress is an important mechanism in the aging process and in the development of age-associated degenerative diseases.
aging is associated with a progressive increase in the production of ROS, and a progressive decrease in mitochondrial function, both of which are likely to be related to oxidative damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial dysfunction is the main factor of aging and that the oxidative stress and the free radicals are the main factors of the mitochondrial dysfunction.
oxidative stress plays an important role during aging.
mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress are two sides of the same coin, and that both contribute to the pathogenesis of aging.
